# 42 Techne — Sovereign Commons Architecture

## Bibliographic identity

Seventeen-page PDF, version 2.0, February 2026. The PDF identifies `4:2 Technè` and the subtitle but no named individual author; preserve corporate authorship unless the title page/source owner supplies a personal byline.

**Provisional full note:** 4:2 Technè, *Sovereign Commons Architecture: A Vision for Community-Led AI Infrastructure*, version 2.0 (February 2026), {page}.

**Submitted bibliography:** withhold until publication status, canonical URL/repository, and preferred authorship are confirmed.

## Essay use

Project report for decentralised, community-led AI infrastructure; local governance; capability leakage; memory and epistemic sovereignty; QL-informed agent architecture; Gebserian integral technology; and a concrete alternative to centralised planetary computation.

**Claim boundary:** this is an affiliated project arm and design proposal that establishes internal architectural provenance. Independent validation of QL and verification of its historical claims require external sources; the architecture itself requires implementation and evaluation records as it matures.

<a id="42-techne-2026-sovereign-commons-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `42-techne-2026-sovereign-commons-q002` — Sessions, knowledge and Agora
^42-techne-2026-sovereign-commons-q002

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** The report describes owner, shared-group and sandboxed sessions; local/remote model routing; persistent community knowledge; and three Agora functions: peer compute brokerage, a wisdom feed and a cooperative host. The proposed wisdom feed carries a P5 artifact into another community’s P0 conditions after selection. These are architectural descriptions, not evidence that cross-community learning or federation ran.
